objective.statement: Learn the minor scales of G, C and F minor, in both forms.
successCriteria: I know G minor has two flats, C minor three and F minor four.
I can write the harmonic and melodic forms of each.
I know the raised notes sometimes need a natural sign.

explanation.text: Three new minor keys have flats in their key signatures. G minor has two (B♭, E♭), C minor has three (B♭, E♭, A♭) and F minor has four (B♭, E♭, A♭, D♭). They are the relative minors of B♭ major, E♭ major and A♭ major.

music.textAlternative: G harmonic minor going up: G, A, B flat, C, D, E flat, F sharp, G.

explanation.caption: G harmonic minor: the 7th, F, is raised to F♯.

music.textAlternative: C melodic minor going up: C, D, E flat, F, G, A, B, C, with A and B natural.

explanation.caption: C melodic minor going up: A♭ and B♭ are raised, to A and B natural.

music.textAlternative: C melodic minor coming down: C, B flat, A flat, G, F, E flat, D, C.

explanation.caption: Coming down: B♭ and A♭, as in the key signature.

music.textAlternative: F harmonic minor going up: F, G, A flat, B flat, C, D flat, E, F.

explanation.caption: F harmonic minor: the 7th, E♭, is raised to E natural.

explanation.text: In a flat key, raising a note often means cancelling a flat: the raised 7th of C minor is B natural, and the raised 7th of F minor is E natural. When the scale is written with its key signature, that raised note needs a natural sign. Raise a flat note by cancelling the flat. Raise a natural note by adding a sharp.

music.textAlternative: C melodic minor scale going up: C, D, E flat, F, G, A, B, C.

steps: Start with C minor: C, D, E flat, F, G, A flat, B flat.
Going up, raise the 6th and 7th: A flat becomes A, and B flat becomes B.
Coming down, bring the flats back: B flat and A flat.
demonstration.textAlternative: C melodic minor going up: with A natural and B natural.
